text: The Sales Director wants to see how a selected territory's sales compare to the company as a whole. That's a benchmark, not just a raw number.

A headline card is meant to show the currently filtered territory's total. A table benchmarks every territory against the company total at once. A territory slicer lets the Sales Director drill into one territory and watch the headline card respond.

This page gets built in one longer, faster pass. The Fields pane now has five measures whose names all start with Total Sales, sitting close together alphabetically, and dragging the wrong one onto a card is an easy, ordinary mistake at this pace.
With no territory filter applied yet, every Total Sales measure agrees, so the headline card looks correct at a glance, whether or not it's actually bound to the right one.
Next lesson covers the Gateway Limitation, a real Power BI fact about scheduling this project's refresh, before the numbers mismatch gets investigated.
